newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures end mixed, March S&P down.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures end mixed, March S&P down.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures ended mixed, with March Standard and Poor's 500 futures lower in late technical weakness in sympathy with Treasury bonds.
June T-bond futures closed on a weak note and near their session lows, sparking profit-taking in March S&Ps and pulling the contract into negative territory.

"We saw a lot of stops and a lot of programs," one S&P 500 futures trader said. "Redbook helped, but the bubble had already burst," he said. March S&Ps rallied as high as psychologically key 800.00 but ran out of steam, letting technical disappointment rule the afternoon, the trader said.
The Redbook Retail Sales Index for February showed U.S. adjusted retail sales up 2.4 percent versus January. That survey was released just before T-bond futures closed.
Stops in March S&PS were noted below 794.90 and 792.00.
"Then we just ran out of time," the trader said. "If we had another hour we'd have new weekly lows."
Several traders said the strong Redbook figure stoked fears of an imminent rate hike.
Comments from Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan last week put U.S. markets on the defensive with warnings of "unsustainable" U.S. stocks and a pre-emptive rate hike.
He delivers his second leg of Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on Wednesday, this time to the House Banking Committee.

"There was a lot of profit-taking and getting out of positions ahead of Greenspan tomorrow," another S&P source said. He said worries centered not on the Fed chief's testimony but on the question and answer period that follows.

U.S. data dragged on T-bonds and stocks briefly early. U.S. January single-family home sales rose 8.6 percent to an annual rate of 870,000 units, against forecasts for 757,000. January leading indicators rose 0.3 percent, with December unrevised at up 0.1 percent.

At the close, March S&P 500s were off 3.20 points at 792.05, KCBT Value Lines rose 0.20 to 709.80, Nikkeis were 120.0 higher at 18,635.0, Midcap rose 1.80 to 264.00, NYSE Composite fell 1.55 to 415.90, and Nasdaq 100s were up 3.50 at 863.25.
